lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: A grid-like arrangement of high-luminance circular pixel clusters. Posterior to the gill slits, these clusters form vertical columns; the first visible column contains 6 spots, with subsequent columns spaced at regular intervals along the longitudinal axis.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Vertical bands of elevated pixel intensity intersect horizontal rows of spots, with the spots functioning as nodes at each intersection point. This creates a distinctive lattice pattern across the mid-lateral region.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: Two prominent horizontal ridges are visible on the upper flank, exhibiting a sharp vertical luminance gradient. The ridges run parallel to the dorsal midline, extending from the gills toward the tail.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The first dorsal fin surface contains approximately 12-15 small, high-luminance spots. These spots are distributed unevenly, with a higher density observed on the posterior and ventral regions of the fin's visible face.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A sharp, vertical linear feature of high pixel intensity is visible crossing the grid pattern immediately posterior to the final gill slit. Irregular high-luminance patches are also present on the leading and distal edges of the right pectoral fin.
other_distinctive_markers: A smaller marine organism, identified as a remora, is visible positioned ventrally to the right pectoral fin.
